sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Mary was a Christian figure with Celtic resonances. When the Roman legions reached Celtic lands, the church absorbed some indigenous spiritual visions into its own. The virgin Mary, mother of Jesus, took on the symbols and stories of a number of Celtic and European mother goddesses. A folk belief in England held that the entire island was Mary's bridal dowry. The dowry was given by her brother, the merchant Joseph of Arimathea, who brought the Grail back to Britain. Some legends say Mary herself lived out her life in Britain after the resurrection of Jesus.
